evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate accepts any nonzero, changed manager PID and changed invocation ID, but does not require the two manager snapshots to belong to the same boot. A guest reboot between the manager restart command and the second inspect changes both fields and satisfies the check, so the report can record an isolated manager restart that was actually a reboot. The reboot snapshots already carry `boot_id`, and requiring nonempty equal manager before/after boot IDs while retaining the PID and invocation-ID checks is a small correctness fix to the intended isolated-restart evidence.
